name: Skat
description: Skat is widely regarded as Germany's national card game and one of the best 3-player trick-taking games ever devised. It features complex bidding based on 'Game Value', a unique trump hierarchy (Jacks are highest), and three main contract types (Suit, Grand, Null). The 'Soloist' plays against two defenders. The game combines luck, skill in hand evaluation, and precise card play.

history.origins: Invented in Altenburg, Thuringia, around 1810 by members of the 'Brommesche Tarok-Gesellschaft'. It combined elements of Tarock (bidding), Schafkopf (Jacks), and L'Hombre (Solitaire).
timeline: 1998: New International Skat Order (ISKO) unifies rules.
history.cultural: Skat is played competitively worldwide, with strict etiquette and complex scoring tables.
history.evolution: The switch from 'TournÃ©' bidding (turning up a card) to 'Reiz' bidding (numerical value) modernized the game.

setup.dealing: Deal 10 cards to each player (3-4-3). 2 cards face-down in the 'Skat' (blind).

rules.objective: Soloist: Score 61+ points (in Suit/Grand) or lose no tricks (Null). Defenders: Prevent Soloist.
rules.gameplay: Soloist can pick up the Skat (Hand game multiplier if they don't). Discard 2 cards. Declare game.
keyRules: Deal 3-4-3; two cards (Skat) face-down to the table. Bidding (Reizen) determines declarer and minimum game value.
Declarer may pick up the Skat and discard two cards, or play Hand without picking up. Declare game type: Suit, Grand, or Null.
Jacks are the highest trumps (J-clubs, J-spades, J-hearts, J-diamonds). Must follow suit; may trump when void. Ten tricks; forehand leads first.
Soloist needs 61+ card points (Suit/Grand) or lose every trick (Null). Card points: A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2; 9-7=0.

strategy.basic: Only bid if you have a strong hand. A good Suit hand needs 5+ trumps including top Jacks. A Grand hand needs 2-3 top Jacks and side Aces. In Null, you need 7s, 8s, 9s in every suit or voids. As a Defender, lead a suit the Soloist is likely void in (long suit) to force a trump, or lead trumps if the Soloist is weak in them (to drain them).
strategy.intermediate: The 'Short Suit' Lead: Against a Suit game, lead a short suit (singleton/doubleton) to try to ruff. But be careful not to free up the Soloist's losers.
strategy.advanced: Counting Matadors: If you have the Jack of Spades (2nd highest) but not the Jack of Clubs, you are 'Without 1'. Game Value = (1+1) * Base. If you pick up the Jack of Clubs from the Skat, you are now 'With 2' (J-Clubs, J-Spades). This changes your multiplier from 2 to 3. Be wary of overbidding if you rely on the Skat.
tips: Jacks are always trumps in Suit/Grand.
Schneider (scoring 90+) and Schwarz (winning all tricks) increase multipliers.
